_what_this_is: A one-use maintainer decision. It states who permitted what, at what cumulative spend, against what cap, and what it does NOT authorize. It deliberately asserts no derived identity: the timestamp, the committed base, the continuation harness digest, both plan hashes and the price are computed by scripts/autoinit/issue_recovery_continuation_authorization.py, which refuses a grant that claims any of them. Consumed by exactly one issuance. The attempt-5 grant and its authorization are SPENT and must not be reused: the checkpoint-path repair moved both the session commit and the continuation harness digest.
granted_by: Maintainer decision, 2026-08-23. 'GO for Recovery Continuation Attempt 6. I reviewed 01be685. The Attempt-5 checkpoint-consumer defect is closed at the right scope. trained_model_dir(out_dir) now resolves the producer's actual contract, out_dir/checkpoints/latest.txt -> out_dir/checkpoints/<tag>/model, and run_probe() delegates to that resolver rather than performing its own path arithmetic. The two post-paid-training failure modes are separately fail-closed. The correction to test_phase_a_stages1_5_execute.py is accepted and important: the harness was not absent; its fake trainer had encoded the defective consumer layout. The fake now emits the same checkpoint tree as Trainer.save_checkpoint(), so the existing end-to-end $0 path can actually catch this defect class. Do not add any further checkpoint abstraction or trained-only retention machinery.' Against last tested implementation 01be685, which is also the pre-authorization HEAD. Since attempt 5 one closure landed and was accepted: THE PROBE CHECKPOINT CONSUMER. Attempt 5 trained its first rung-1 probe for 61.7 minutes and then died reading it, because run_probe read out_dir/latest.txt and out_dir/<tag>/model while Trainer.save_checkpoint writes out_dir/checkpoints/latest.txt and checkpoints/<tag>/model -- one writer, two consumers, and only this one wrong. The repair is a driver-local resolver plus a targeted regression over a synthetic real-layout tree. Critically, the earlier claim that no $0 path executed the line was WRONG and the truth was worse: tests/pod/test_phase_a_stages1_5_execute.py does execute run_probe end to end, and passed only because its fake trainer wrote the layout the DRIVER expected rather than the trainer's. The full suite went red the moment the driver was corrected. The fake now writes the real tree, and reintroducing the driver defect against it makes that harness fail 1+14, so the defect class is now catchable at $0. Verified on the current tree: full suite 2176 passed / 12 skipped, +4 with the skip count unchanged; frozen-asset verifier passed with no problems; 5 mutations each turning a passing state into a failing one, including the 15-minute end-to-end one. The continuation harness digest moved 95cf336d -> 0dbf1272.
covers: One (1) launch of the AutoInitializer Phase-A RECOVERY CONTINUATION, attempt 6, on a single NVIDIA L40S at no more than $0.99/h. It imports the verified Attempt-12 Stage-1 result -- the five preserved selected leaves, in the committed selected order, re-identified from the bytes that actually arrive on the pod -- and runs recovery Stages 2 through 5 under the frozen science, the existing watchdog, soft-stop, hard-stop, artifact-gate and provider-confirmed teardown behaviour. Everything ahead of Stage 2 is already demonstrated on paid hardware and is not revisited: the transport (attempts 3 and 4), Stage 0 attestation and the strict Stage-1 import with control measurement and admission (attempts 4 and 5), and the release/headroom contracts (attempt 5, freed_allocated_bytes 8,101,709,824 and 43.87 GiB free against the 43.65 GiB gate). Attempt 5 also trained one rung-1 probe in 61.7 minutes against the 61.55 priced; that probe was lost with its pod and is NOT resumable scientific work, so this attempt starts recovery normally from the preserved Stage-1 inputs and retrains it. Authorized pricing is DERIVED from continuation_budget(), not written: expected $14.9233, per-launch hard ceiling $16.7456, which is also the hard cap. The beam search is not run, not reconstructed, and is structurally unreachable from this harness.

does_not_authorize: Adding any further checkpoint abstraction, or trained-but-unscored cross-session retention machinery. Rerunning or redesigning Stage 1. Revisiting the transport. Altering the verified memory-release or headroom contracts, including RECOVERY_TRAINER_BYTES, require_released and require_headroom, and in particular lowering any threshold to make a launch succeed or avoid a refusal. Changing the frozen recovery recipe, KD chunk, microbatch, dtype, optimizer, trainer implementation or the selection rules. Repairing and relaunching on a live pod. A beam search, a fresh Stage 1, or any reconstruction of the search. Re-ranking or re-selecting the five leaves, or changing their committed order. Retraining the permanent controls. Measuring the canonical control more than once or on anything but the frozen Stage-1 suite. Any new canary, rehearsal, readiness, measurement, calibration, architecture, pricing or harness expansion. Any additional storage cleanup, including the 32 sole-copy remote objects totalling 69.671 GiB or the two protected wheelhouses. Increasing the cumulative cap. Any follow-on or automatically started session. Reopening the frozen science: science plan 02be33b9, session plan 9377a2dc, Stage-3 protocol 250f72ef, equivalence interval 0.011695296982299022, feasibility floor 0.3, tokenizer 7781771acc3798ee, recovery fingerprint ab0d8cfd, the seed and conditional-sc policy, the operator ids and declared mathematics. Reusing any spent grant or authorization from attempts 1 through 5. Any other paid session. Treating the remaining cumulative headroom as authorization beyond this one launch.
fail_closed_instruction: On any new material failure: preserve the full traceback and the stage artifacts, fail closed, collect evidence through the existing supported path, obtain provider-confirmed teardown, and return for review. Do not repair on the live pod and do not relaunch. A refusal by require_released() or require_headroom() after Stage 1 remains the INTENDED fail-closed result of the attempt-4 repair rather than a failure of the run, and neither gate may be weakened to avoid it. The five imported Stage-1 leaves are session INPUTS: they are not re-derived, not modified, and their canonical off-pod copies in the dev-box checkpoint store remain the durable record regardless of what happens in Stages 2-5.
on_completion: Report rung-1 results, rung-2 results, whether the conditional seed-sc rung fired, the final selection, retained artifacts, actual spend and provider-confirmed teardown, together with commits and hashes, authorization identity, bundle round-trip and pod lifecycle. Tear the pod down as soon as the run reaches a terminal state rather than waiting for a backstop, and confirm teardown with the provider. Then STOP. Do not self-authorize any subsequent session. Two non-material bookkeeping items are to be normalized in the post-attempt state update rather than before launch: the trained_model_dir docstring still says no $0 path executes this consumer, which the corrected end-to-end fake now does, and current_state.json.baseline_commit is stale relative to its own latest_verification.
